sanskrit_verse: माषो विंशतिभागस्तु ज्ञेयः कार्षापणस्य तु। काकणी तु चतुर्भागो माषस्य च पणस्य च॥
transliteration: māṣo viṃśatibhāgas tu jñeyaḥ kārṣāpaṇasya tu | kākaṇī tu caturbhāgo māṣasya ca paṇasya ca ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One māṣa is known as one-twentieth part of a kārṣāpaṇa; one kākaṇī is one-fourth part of a māṣa and one paṇa.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in precise quantification as defined by SPH
Causation aligns with measurable proportionality in transactional dharma
Capacity-based responsibility requires understanding of standardized units
Restoration logic depends on exact restitution according to unit value
Consciousness alignment occurs through adherence to fixed economic truths

supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes the threshold of financial precision required for determining liability and restitution. The court must apply these fixed ratios as authoritative measures, not subject to interpretation or market fluctuation. Responsibility arises from deviation from these defined units, not intent.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through standardized measurement. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential alignment to base units—kārṣāpaṇa → māṣa → kākaṇī. Responsibility is proportional to misalignment from the defined structure. There is no punitive consequence; correction restores transactional integrity and consciousness alignment.
